2. Detoured the four constructors 6.1 left out (CompanionBehavior, RandomInteractionBehavior, SpawnLocationBehavior with no stack argument, WalkPathBehavior with one), traced the sequence and combat constructors, WaypointVector::push_back and the death removal site 0x60E04B; watched the creature count and the player's hp
3. `console behavior_proto:cases` (the development mod, hand-built objects: a block from operator_new zeroed, the game's constructor, the children appended, cube::Creature.behavior written, the creature's spawn_pos (+0x1C0) set to its position). Twelve friendly slimes (hostile type 3, which the player cannot hurt) around the player: a control with no behaviour, RandomWalk alone (no sequence), Seq[SpawnLocation, RandomWalk], Seq[LookAt] 10 blocks away and 4 blocks away, Seq[RandomInteraction] 10 and 4 blocks away, Seq[WalkPath] (a 5-block square, 16 blocks away; a 3-block square, 4 blocks away), Seq[Combat, WalkPath] (the guard shape), a Seq[WalkPath] with one waypoint 6 blocks from its spawn, and Seq[Combat, Companion] whose owner is the player's creature id (1), 12 blocks away. The mod logs each creature every 40 ticks (about 12 s under Wine): position, distance from its spawn, body_yaw, hp, distance and bearing to the player, and the behaviour object's words
4. The mod's own clock (the console steps of a replay land 8 to 60 s late): after 170 s it writes hp 0 into every case but the companion; after 200 s it spawns a hostile slime (hostile type 1, level 1) with a lone CombatBehavior (no sequence) 6 blocks north-east of the player and writes hp 0 into it 35 s later; the companion gets hp 0 10 s after that. Before the kill the script gave the player input: hold d 5 s, hold a 10 s, hold d 5 s (the player walked about 10 blocks east, then 44 west and back)
5. Five runs, kept in the evidence folder (run1 to run4 beside the final files): 1 had no kill or combat phase (its console steps never landed); 2 killed the cases (the death site was hit) but the combat phase failed on int64 coordinates; 3 ran the combat phase; runs 1 to 3 read heap garbage in the fields the constructors do not write (WalkPath +0x14, Companion +4), so the mod now zeroes each block first; 4 is the first with zeroed blocks; 5 (the record) keeps the companion alive for the combat phase

Observations:

- the four new constructors ran without a fault as detours (Companion 1 call, RandomInteraction 5, SpawnLocation 4, WalkPath 31 with the stack argument 2.0f; the counts include the zone generators' own creatures except Companion, which only the mod built), WaypointVector::push_back 519 calls, the sequence and combat constructors 55 (Combat, incl. two of the mod's); the death removal site ran 14 times after the kills; the hooks were all removed at the end
- every object the mod built was stepped by the game: no fault in any of the five runs, and the game ran on after every kill (the destructor frees the sequence's block only, as 6.1 read: the children and the WalkPath's vector are not freed by it, a leak per creature, not a fault)
- CombatBehavior alone (no sequence) as cube::Creature.behavior works: the hostile slime went from 6 blocks to 2.2 blocks of the player within the first sample, then followed the player (0.1 to 1.2 blocks in the next samples); the player's hp fell from 265 to 167.6 and 23.6 in run 5 (to 0 in run 3). The object's words: +4 a countdown (0x4BC1, 0x18C6, then 0), +8 = 0x41A00000 (20.0f) all the time, +0xC 0x25F once (a state), +0x10 0
- CompanionBehavior: with the owner id written at +8 (the player's id, 1; +0xC 0; +4 zero from the zeroed block) the friendly slime walked from 12 blocks to 2.0 to 3.0 blocks of the player and stayed there, and when the player moved it followed (26.9 blocks from its spawn while the player was 44 blocks west, then back to 2 blocks); it fights what the player fights: in run 5 the hostile slime's hp went 100, 99.3, 15.4, 1.5 while the player stood still and the companion attacked it (the companion's hp fell to 15.9 and it was knocked 26.8 blocks from its spawn); the hostile slime hit the player too (265 to 23.6). The child Combat's +4 counted down like a lone CombatBehavior's
- RandomWalkBehavior alone (no sequence) works: the friendly slime wandered up to 32 to 35 blocks from its spawn (mean 9 to 11), yaw changing at every sample; its +4 is a changing counter. The control (no behaviour) stayed within 0.5 to 1.6 blocks of its spawn with yaw 0
- Seq[SpawnLocation, RandomWalk]: the creature wandered as far as the lone RandomWalk (mean 10 to 14 blocks, at most 31 to 34 blocks from its spawn) although its spawn_pos (+0x1C0) was set: no pull towards the home position was visible up to 34 blocks; the object has no state (4 bytes). Either the class pulls only from farther, or it needs another condition, or it is inert as the first child
- LookAtPlayerBehavior in a sequence turns the creature: the slime 4 blocks north of the player had body_yaw -180.0 (facing south, at the player, bearing 180) and followed the player round (yaw -131 at bearing 125); the one 10 blocks away stayed at yaw 0.0 (as the control) and turned at 8.8 blocks (once the player came nearer), not at 9.6 blocks and beyond: the range is about 9 blocks
- RandomInteractionBehavior in a sequence did nothing that shows: yaw 0.0 and the position unchanged (up to 2 blocks of settling) over about 240 s at 4 and 10 blocks, +4 zero all the time, no change of the name tag or the [R] TALK prompt (every hostile-3 creature has it); the villagers' talk is not from this class, as the strings suggested
- WalkPathBehavior with a hand-built path works once its +0x14 is zero (the copy constructor 0x58B860 zeroes it, the constructor 0x58B8A0 does not): the waypoint index at +0x10 counted 0, 1, 2, 3 (the four corners) for the 5-block and the 3-block square and for the guard's Seq[Combat, WalkPath], the creature turned (yaw changed at 11 to 17 samples) and stayed within 3.5 to 6.9 blocks of its spawn (the square's diagonal is 7.1 blocks), and +0x14 was a timer of some thousand units (up to 0x13C3) that counted down to 0 while the creature stood at a waypoint; the vector at +4 held begin, end and capacity 96 bytes apart for four waypoints (24 bytes each), the float at +0x18 stayed 2.0f. The Seq[WalkPath] with one waypoint 6 blocks south of the creature's spawn walked 4.3 to 5.0 blocks towards it with yaw 178 (facing south) and stopped, index 0 all the time. Runs 1 to 3 (the block not zeroed) showed +0x14 as garbage, a tiny float or a small integer, and the creature did not walk in runs 1 and 2
- the creature's own field the recipe leaves out: +0x1C0 (spawn_pos in the layout) is the SpawnLocationBehavior's home; the loader's recipe does not set it (the zone path copies the Spawn's position there), and 8.3's spawn has to set it for the kinds that read it

3. Phase 2, the monster: `console config entity_spawner fights true`, then the same spawn; 14 samples 8 s apart (the console steps land 20 to 60 s late under Wine); the player's hp watched; the lowest id's `behavior` (+0x13E4) read

Observations:

- the mod logged `spawned Green slime (type 37, hostile 1, level 1, behavior still), id -1` for phase 1 and `... behavior monster), id -2` for phase 2: the spawner sent behavior = "still" or "monster" from its `fights` option to kyubu.game.creature_spawn on the server side, which built the creature with the loader's recipe
- phase 1, the control: the creature with the lowest id (low word 0xFFFFFFFF, hp 100) had behavior 0 at +0x13E4, stood at the same x and y in all 8 samples over about 100 s (four blocks south of the player: y 544482138 against 544744282, in world units) and the player's hp stayed 265 (the php watch: 10,033 samples, 0 changes)
- phase 2, the monster: the lowest id was now 0xFFFFFFFE (hp 100) with a non-zero behavior pointer (656585232, a cube::SequentialBehavior block from operator_new) and it was next to the player at the first sample after the spawn (2.5 blocks), then 1.7, 1.4, 1.9 and 0.1 blocks in the next four, following the player as the hits pushed it about 16 blocks north in 8 s each time; the player's hp fell 265 to 225.6, 158.7, 106.7, 50.3 and 0 in five samples (the php watch: 118 changes, first 265, last 0). Before the creature landed the four samples of phase 2 showed hp 265 and the control at rest
- the first replay (the monster spawned first, run 1) showed the same: 01-spawned.png (run1-01-spawned.png) has the player at 181/265 with red damage numbers over its head 30 s after the console step, and run1-02-approach.png the player at 0/265 with `[R] REVIVE`. Its slime had hp 100 all along (nothing hurt it), and was gone at the end, as the game removes creatures away from a dead player
- 01-control.png (265/265, the console closed) and 02-monster.png and 03-monster-later.png (the console still open: gamepilot types a line in a second or two, so the shots were taken while the console steps ran) do not show the slime; the numbers above are the evidence
- no error or fault in any of the three runs; the probe's hooks were all removed at the end (hooks == 0); run 2 failed only on its own control check (the spawn had not landed when the script read it), so phase 1 was made the control first and the waits longer

| Confirms | Observed |
|---|---|
| [`cube::Creature.behavior`](types/cube_Creature.md) | the creature spawned with behavior = "monster" held a non-zero sequence pointer at +0x13E4, the one spawned with "still" held 0; the World step drove the first (it came to the player and hit it, hp 265 to 0 in about 40 s under Wine) and left the second where it stood |

## teleport-check

- **Build:** Cube.exe (`cube-0x51D2CE9C`)
- **Kyubu:** 1.0.1
- **Date:** 2026-10-03

Steps:

1. Wine replay: gamepilot made the character Tester and a new world with the mods teleport and level_rework beside kyubu_probe; waited 20 s there
2. the input turned dev_commands on, listed the level-61 dungeons (`teleport:tp dungeons 61`), went to the nearest (`teleport:tp dungeon 61`, hovering), took a screenshot, landed, took a screenshot and ran `level_rework:levels creatures`

Observations:

- Wine replays 5 and 7 passed, no fault. The player starts at x 8396928, y 8396928, z 215.1 (blocks, 65,536 units per block). Writing cube::CreatureData.pos moves the player: `teleport:tp rel 60 0` gave x 8396988 and the player stood on the ground at z 219.1 four seconds later; `teleport:tp rel 3000 1000` (run 5) gave x 8399988, y 8397928, hovered at z 250 and the screenshot shows terrain the start does not have. After `teleport:tp land` the player stayed at z 253.1: the ground there is about 253. Replay 3 (a 3,000-block hop that kept z 215, before the hover rule) left the player at z 235.1 with the start scene still on screen: no zone was loaded where it landed
- dungeon positions (run 6 dumped the raw data of the 9 regions the new world builds, with no level_rework): a region's 64 missions (+0x14018, 0x68 bytes) hold the dungeons as kind 0xE; the mission's origin (u64 x at +0, u64 y at +8, 65,536 per block) is the centre of the dungeon's zone tile. It equals the tile position computed from the tile index a*64+b of the 4096 zone tiles (kind byte 3): x = (row*64 + a)*256 + 128 blocks, y = (column*64 + b)*256 + 128, in all three regions compared (48 dungeons, levels matching one to one)
- run 7, with level_rework loaded: `teleport:tp dungeons 61` listed 9 level-61 dungeons of 144 built, the nearest 8034 blocks away at x 8400000, y 8389504; `teleport:tp dungeon 61` hovered there at z 250; after `teleport:tp land` the HUD read CATACOMBS OF ASTAR and the screen was the dark inside of a dungeon (02-landed.png), z 241.1. `levels creatures` then listed 94 creatures, levels 1 to 61, 0 outside 1-100: SKELETON (17) 4, UNDEAD_MALE (15) 26, UNDEAD_FEMALE (16) 41 and ZOMBIE (96) 7 are all level 61 with +p 2; BAT (59) 3 and the chests (143) 3 are level 61 with +p 0; the others (types 87, 98, 105, 120, 127, 132, 135 and the player) are outside the dungeon, levels 1 to 39
- the console command is `teleport:tp` (a name needs the mod's namespace); output goes to the console and to the log

| Confirms | Observed |
|---|---|
| [`cube::World.joined`](types/cube_World.md) | 0 in single-player |

## trap-body

- **Build:** Cube.exe (`cube-0x51D2CE9C`)
- **Kyubu:** 1.0.1
- **Date:** 2026-10-17

Steps:

1. Wine replay: gamepilot makes the character Tester (human male warrior) and a new world; waits 15 s there; the body yaw is set to 0
2. `spawner PINK_SLIME 1 still` puts one slime 4 blocks north of the player; it is the carrier (the newest creature)
3. `trap_proto:run`: the carrier is put 2 blocks east and 2 north of the player, 1.5 up, and given 5 blocks/s north and 6 up; every World step it is logged; when it lands after a fall faster than 1.5 its vertical velocity is written back as 0.55 times the fastest fall seen (a Lua bounce); the hide mask (draw_creature argument 9, [ESP+0x20] at creature_draw_site) is 0xFFFFFFFF; at +6 s its hp is set to 0
4. shots: at rest and hidden, and after the hp write
5. runs 1 to 4 (the same probe, earlier timelines): throw with and without the bounce; the draw colour's alpha at 0, 0.35 and the green and blue at 0; the hide mask at 0xFFFFFFFF; the creature's scale (+0x80) at 0.02

Observations:

- the game's physics moves a creature that stands still: a velocity written at Creature+0x34 (blocks a second) carries it, gravity pulls it down about 30 blocks/s^2 (6 up at 5 blocks/s north: apex 0.5 s later, ground at 0.63 s), the on-ground bit (Creature+0x5C bit 0, flags 0x11) comes up at the landing and the ground friction brings 5 blocks/s to 0 in about 1.5 s (thrown at 5 blocks/s north and 6 up from 1.5 above the ground: with no bounce it rests 4.0 blocks from where it started, with two bounces 5.3 blocks); the creature stops dead (velocity 0.00 for the next 4 s)
- a bounce by a Lua write works: at the landing the vertical velocity was written upward (0.55 times the fall speed of 11.7 blocks/s: 6.4, then 2.6 after the second landing) and the creature rose again and landed twice; one throw of the first four runs missed its landing because the fall speed was read from the step before the landing; run 5 keeps the fastest fall seen and landed both bounces
- the creature's draw colour alpha is not an opacity: alpha 0 darkened the pink slime to dark purple and 0.35 left it nearly as pink as 1 (runs 1 to 3 shots 07 and 09); green and blue at 0 only darken it
- the hide mask of draw_creature works: with 0xFFFFFFFF written at [ESP+0x20] of creature_draw_site the slime is not drawn (run 4 shot 04-mask-rest and run 5 shot 02-rest-hidden against the pink slime beside the bow in runs 3 and 4); the value before the write was 0
- the creature's scale at AppearanceData.scale (Creature+0x80, read 0.8 on the carrier) written to 0.016 each step did not make it vanish (run 4 shot 07: the slime is still drawn): that copy is not what the draw reads
- hp set to 0 on the carrier at rest: the creature was gone from the map by the next lookup (the same millisecond of the log), no error and no corpse in the shot (run 5 shot 03); the player's XP stayed 0/50
- a creature spawned by entity_spawner (hostile type 1, behaviour still) was used; the player attacks and the AI of monsters were not tried on it
- replay 5 passed, 1 of 1 expectations held; the four trap_proto hooks installed; the slime was drawn through the first draw site (0x4B5D8C, `draw_a` 43 to 144 passes), the later passes (0x4BA8D8, 0x4BA97F) never ran

| Confirms | Observed |
|---|---|
| [`creature_draw_site`](creatures.md) | the stack argument 9 of draw_creature at [ESP+0x20] (hide mask) set to 0xFFFFFFFF hides the creature; the colour vec4 at [ESP+0x14] alpha only darkens |
